The ruler of the realm is sending an emissary to a hostile neighbor to negotiate a truce, and the emissary needs protection.
A castle or city has been drawn into another plane of existence.
A storm tears across the land, with a mysterious flying citadel in the eye of the storm.
A band of hunting giants has driven its prey—enormous beasts—into pastureland.
Evil cultists gather from around the world to summon a monstrous god or alien entity.
A long-lost journal describes an incredible journey to a hidden subterranean realm full of magical wonders.
During a drought, low water levels in a lake reveal previously unknown ancient ruins that contain a powerful evil.
A tyrannical ruler outlaws the use of magic without official sanction. A secret society of spellcasters seeks to oust the tyrant.
A portal to the Abyss opens in a cursed location and spews demons into the world.
Cultists hope to persuade a dragon to undergo the rite that will transform it into a dracolich.
An adult dragon’s lair is transforming an expanse into an environment inhospitable to the other creatures living there.
Two parts of a magic item are in the hands of bitter enemies; the third piece is lost.
An innocent person is being framed for the crimes of a shape-shifting monster.
To take revenge against a village for an imagined slight, a necromancer has been animating the corpses in the village cemetery.
Wererats living in a city’s sewers plot to take control of the governing council.
After a local fisher pulls a grotesque statue from the sea, aquatic monsters start attacking the waterfront at night.
A hag’s curse is making animals unusually aggressive.
A new sinkhole has revealed a long-buried dungeon thought to hold treasure.
A pack of gnolls is rampaging dangerously close to local farmlands.
An abandoned house on the edge of town is haunted by Undead because of a cursed item in the house.
Bandit activity signals efforts to revive an evil cult long ago driven from the region.
Creatures from the Feywild enter the world and cause mischief and misfortune among villagers and their livestock.
Miners discovered an underground ruin and were captured by monsters living there.
Bullies have appointed themselves the village militia and are extorting money and food from villagers.
A contagion in a forest is causing spiders to grow massive and become aggressive.
The ruins on the hill near the village lie under a curse, so people don’t go there—except a scholar who wants to study the ruins.
Ghouls are venturing out of the catacombs at night.
A notorious criminal hides from the law in an old ruin or abandoned mine.
A new captain has taken charge of a band of pirates or bandits and started raiding more frequently.
A dragon wyrmling has gathered a band of kobolds to help it amass a hoard.
An evil cult is spreading in a village. Those who oppose the cult are marked for sacrifice.
A rivalry between two merchant families escalates from mischief to mayhem.
A titan imprisoned in the Underdark begins to break free, causing terrible earthquakes that are only a hint of the destruction that the titan will cause if it is released.
A band of giants drove away a metallic dragon and took over the dragon’s lair, and the dragon wants to reclaim the lair.
A holy temple was built around a portal leading to one of the Lower Planes to prevent any evil from passing through in either direction. Now the temple has come under siege from both directions.
Five ancient metallic dragons lair in the Pillars of Creation. If all these dragons are killed, the world will collapse into chaos. One has just been slain.
An ancient hero returns from the dead to prepare the world for the return of an equally ancient monster.
An ancient Artifact has the power to defeat or imprison a rampaging titan.
An ancient dragon is scheming to destroy a god and take the god’s place in the pantheon. The dragon’s minions are searching for Artifacts that can summon and weaken this god.
A god of agriculture is angry, causing rivers to dry up and crops to wither.
A lich tries to exterminate any spellcasters that approach the lich’s level of power.
An Artifact belonging to a god falls into mortal hands.

Just when the characters think the main threat is defeated, it transforms into a different monster or a more powerful form.
A villain and two or three lieutenants perform separate rites in a large room. The adventurers must disrupt all the rites.
The adventurers must choose whether to pursue a fleeing villain or save an NPC they care about or a group of innocents.
The adventurers confront a villain and a group of minions in a battle to the finish.
An ally betrays the adventurers as they’re about to achieve their goal. (Use this climax carefully, and don’t overuse it.)
The adventurers chase a villain while dodging obstacles designed to thwart them, leading to a final confrontation in the villain’s refuge.
The actions of the adventurers or a villain result in a cataclysmic event that the adventurers must escape.
The adventurers race to the site where a villain is bringing a master plan to its conclusion, arriving just as that plan is about to be completed.
A portal opens to another plane of existence. Creatures on the other side spill out, forcing the adventurers to close the portal while dealing with a villain at the same time.
The dungeon begins to collapse while a villain attempts to escape in the chaos.
Have travelers bring news of events transpiring elsewhere, leading characters toward the new adventure.
Introduce a person, an object, or information that the characters need to transport safely to a location involved in the new adventure.

Give the characters a treasure that’s wrapped in mystery they’ll need to unravel in the new adventure.

Have a major villain flee to a location that features in the new adventure. The characters might be able to pursue the villain, or they might have to search for clues about where the villain has gone.

A nest of [[/r 1d4 + 3#Rainbow-colored eggs]] rainbow-colored eggs springs up. Any creature that eats an egg makes a [[/save ability=con dc=20 format=long]]. On a successful save, a creature permanently increases its lowest ability score by 1, randomly choosing among equally low scores. On a failed save, the creature takes [[/damage 10d6 type=force]] damage from an internal explosion.
A giant beanstalk sprouts, growing to a height of the DM’s choice. The top leads where the DM chooses, such as to a great view, a cloud giant’s castle, or another plane of existence.

A fruit tree grows. It has [[/r 1d10 + 20#Pieces of fruit]] fruit, [[/gmr 1d8#Fruits acting as Potions]] of which act as randomly determined potions. The tree vanishes after 1 hour. Picked fruit remains, retaining any magic for 30 days.
A geyser erupts and spouts water, beer, mayonnaise, tea, vinegar, wine, or oil (DM’s choice) 30 feet into the air for [[/r 1d4#Geyser duration (minutes)]] minutes.

Fey. The item is exquisitely crafted from the finest materials and glows with a pale radiance in moonlight, shedding Dim Light in a 5-foot radius. Any metal in the item is silver or mithral rather than iron or steel.
Elemental Earth. This item might be crafted from stone. Any cloth or leather elements are studded with finely polished rock.
Dragon. This item incorporates precious metals and gems from a dragon’s hoard. It grows warm when within 120 feet of a Dragon.
Devotees of Lolth. The item is half the normal weight. It is inscribed with spiders and webs in honor of Lolth.
Elemental Fire. This item is warm to the touch, and any metal parts are crafted from black iron. Flame imagery covers its surface.
Elf. The item is half the normal weight. It is adorned with symbols of nature: leaves, vines, stars, and the like.
Elemental Water. Lustrous fish scales replace leather or cloth on this item, and seashells and worked coral (as hard as any metal) replace metal portions.
Giant. The item is larger than normal and was crafted by Giants for use by their smaller allies.

Fiend. The item is made of iron or horn, and any cloth or leather components are crafted from the hide of Fiends. Leering faces or vile runes are engraved on its surface. Celestials find it repulsive.
Gnome. The item is crafted to appear ordinary and well used. It could also incorporate gears and mechanical components, even if these aren’t essential to its function.
Dwarf. The item is durable and has Dwarvish runes worked into its design. It might be associated with a clan that would like to see it returned to their ancestral halls.
Elemental Air. The item is half the normal weight and feels hollow. If it’s made of fabric, it is diaphanous.
Aberration. The item is ancient. At a glance, it seems to be covered with mucus.
Undead. The item incorporates symbols of death, such as bones and skulls, and it might be crafted from parts of corpses. It feels cold to the touch.

Heroic. A great hero once wielded this item. Anyone who knows the item’s history expects great deeds from the new owner.
Symbol of Power. This item was once used as part of royal regalia or as a badge of high office.
Arcane. This item was created for an ancient order of spellcasters and bears the order’s symbol.
Ornament. The item honors a special event. Inset gemstones, gold or platinum inlays, and gold or silver filigree adorn its surface.
Prophecy. The item features in a prophecy: its bearer is destined to play a key role in future events.
Religious. This item was used in religious ceremonies dedicated to a particular deity. It has religious symbols worked into it.
Sinister. This item is linked to a deed of great evil, such as a massacre or an assassination. It might have a name or be closely associated with a villain who used it.
Delver. While underground, you always know the item’s depth below the surface and the direction to the nearest staircase, ramp, or other path leading upward.
Unbreakable. The item can’t be broken. Special means must be used to destroy it.
Guardian. The item warns you, granting a +2 bonus to your Initiative rolls if you don’t have the Incapacitated condition.
Waterborne. This item floats on water and other liquids. You have Advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks to swim.
Strange Material. The item was created from a material that is bizarre given its purpose. Its durability is unaffected.
Beacon. You can take a Bonus Action to cause the item to shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet, or to extinguish the light.
Sentinel. The DM chooses a kind of creature, such as mind flayers or trolls. This item glows faintly when such creatures are within 120 feet of it.
Compass. You can take a Magic action to learn which way is magnetic north. Nothing happens if this property is used in a location that has no magnetic north.
Harmonious. Attuning to this item takes only 1 minute.
War Leader. You can take a Magic action to cause your voice or signal to carry clearly for up to 600 feet until the end of your next turn.
Secret Message. A message is hidden somewhere on the item. It might be visible only at a certain time, under the light of one phase of the moon, or in a specific location.
Songcraft. Whenever this item is struck or is used to strike a foe, you hear a fragment of an ancient song.
Key. The item is used to unlock a container, chamber, vault, or door.
Temperate. You are unharmed by temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, and 100 degrees Fahrenheit or higher.
Metamorphic. The item periodically alters its appearance in slight ways. You have no control over these minor alterations, which have no effect on the item’s use.
Confident. The item helps you feel self-assured.
Covetous. You become obsessed with material wealth.
Fragile. The item crumbles, frays, chips, or cracks slightly when wielded, worn, or activated. This quirk has no effect on its properties.
Blissful. You feel fortunate and optimistic about what the future holds. Butterflies and other harmless creatures might frolic in the item’s presence.
Repulsive. You feel a sense of distaste when in contact with the item and continue to experience discomfort while bearing it.
Loud. The item makes a loud noise—such as a clang, a shout, or a resonating gong—when used.
Painful. You experience a harmless flash of pain when using the item.
